```{r}
#| label: load-packages-r
#| include: false
library(tidyverse)
library(nanoparquet)
library(tidymodels)
library(scales)
library(patchwork)

# The factor zoo of lecture 10 and exercise 7
sample_start <- ymd("1973-01-01")
sample_end <- ymd("2023-12-31")
test_start <- ymd("2000-01-01")
estimation_years <- paste0(year(sample_start), "–", year(test_start) - 1)
test_years <- paste0(year(test_start), "–", year(sample_end))

# Penalties of lecture 10 and the number of folds. The figures before the
# cross-validation slide need the folds; that slide's code defines them again
ridge_lambdas <- 10^seq(-7, -1, by = 0.25)
lasso_lambdas <- 10^seq(-6, -2.5, by = 0.25)
n_folds <- 5

months_per_year <- 12

# Colours of the slides, used by the figures
ku_red <- "#901A1E"
jet <- "#3d3d3d"
grey <- "#666666"
light <- "#e6e3df"
theme_set(
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14) + theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank())
)

source("lecture-slides/_live-poll.R")
components_poll <- "aef27-l11-pc-lasso"
components_choices <- c(
  "1 to 5",
  "6 to 20",
  "21 to 50",
  "51 to 100",
  "More than 100"
)
```

```{python}
#| label: load-packages-py
#| include: false
import numpy as np
from sklearn.base import clone
from sklearn.model_selection import GridSearchCV, GroupKFold
```

```{r}
#| label: lecture-10-code
#| include: false
# The data, the metric and the workflows of lecture 10
osap_url <- paste0(
  "https://huggingface.co/datasets/OpenSourceAP/CrossSection/resolve/",
  "Data-Release-2026.10/Portfolios/Full%20Sets%20OP/PredictorLSretWide.parquet"
)
osap_file <- "data/osap_long_short_returns.parquet"
if (!file.exists(osap_file)) {
  download.file(osap_url, osap_file, mode = "wb")
}
anomalies <- read_parquet(osap_file) |>
  filter(between(date, sample_start, sample_end)) |>
  select(date, where(\(x) !anyNA(x))) |>
  mutate(across(-date, \(x) x / 100), y = 1)
anomaly_names <- setdiff(names(anomalies), c("date", "y"))
sample_split <- make_splits(
  filter(anomalies, date < test_start),
  assessment = filter(anomalies, date >= test_start)
)
estimation_months <- training(sample_split)
test_months <- testing(sample_split)

sharpe_ratio_vec <- function(truth, estimate, ...) {
  mean(estimate) / sd(estimate) * sqrt(months_per_year)
}
sharpe_ratio <- function(data, truth, estimate, ...) {
  numeric_metric_summarizer(
    "sharpe_ratio",
    sharpe_ratio_vec,
    data,
    !!enquo(truth),
    !!enquo(estimate)
  )
}
sharpe_ratio <- new_numeric_metric(sharpe_ratio, direction = "maximize")
sharpe_in <- function(fit, months) {
  augment(fit, months) |> sharpe_ratio(y, .pred) |> pull(.estimate)
}
# Sharpe ratios of a fitted workflow in both samples, for figures and tables
sample_sharpe <- function(fit) {
  c(
    estimation = sharpe_in(fit, estimation_months),
    test = sharpe_in(fit, test_months)
  )
}

plug_in_workflow <- workflow() |>
  add_variables(outcomes = y, predictors = all_of(anomaly_names)) |>
  add_model(linear_reg(), formula = y ~ 0 + .)
ridge_model <- linear_reg(penalty = tune(), mixture = 0) |>
  set_engine(
    "glmnet",
    intercept = FALSE,
    standardize = FALSE,
    path_values = ridge_lambdas,
    control = list(thresh = 1e-12)
  )
ridge_workflow <- update_model(plug_in_workflow, ridge_model)
lasso_model <- linear_reg(penalty = tune(), mixture = 1) |>
  set_engine(
    "glmnet",
    intercept = FALSE,
    standardize = FALSE,
    path_values = lasso_lambdas,
    control = list(thresh = 1e-12)
  )
lasso_workflow <- update_model(plug_in_workflow, lasso_model)

# A penalty in text: 10⁻⁴ or 3.2 × 10⁻⁴
penalty_text <- function(x) {
  exponent <- floor(log10(x) + 1e-9)
  mantissa <- signif(x / 10^exponent, 2)
  power <- paste0("10", chartr("-0123456789", "⁻⁰¹²³⁴⁵⁶⁷⁸⁹", exponent))
  if (mantissa == 1) power else paste(mantissa, "×", power)
}

market <- read_parquet("data/factors_ff3_monthly.parquet") |>
  filter(between(date, sample_start, sample_end))
market_sharpe <- c(
  estimation = sharpe_ratio_vec(
    estimate = market$mkt_excess[market$date < test_start]
  ),
  test = sharpe_ratio_vec(
    estimate = market$mkt_excess[market$date >= test_start]
  )
)
equal_sharpe <- c(
  estimation = sharpe_ratio_vec(
    estimate = rowMeans(estimation_months[anomaly_names])
  ),
  test = sharpe_ratio_vec(estimate = rowMeans(test_months[anomaly_names]))
)
plug_in_sharpe <- sample_sharpe(fit(plug_in_workflow, estimation_months))
ridge_path <- tibble(lambda = ridge_lambdas) |>
  mutate(
    fit = map(lambda, \(lambda) {
      ridge_workflow |>
        finalize_workflow(tibble(penalty = lambda)) |>
        fit(estimation_months)
    }),
    estimation = map_dbl(fit, \(fit) sharpe_in(fit, estimation_months)),
    test = map_dbl(fit, \(fit) sharpe_in(fit, test_months))
  )
```

## Which penalty?

- **Lecture 10:** `r length(anomaly_names)` anomalies, estimation sample `r estimation_years`, test sample `r test_years`. The plug-in portfolio falls from `r number(plug_in_sharpe[["estimation"]], 0.01)` to `r number(plug_in_sharpe[["test"]], 0.01)`
- Ridge earns a Sharpe ratio between `r number(min(ridge_path$test), 0.01)` and `r number(max(ridge_path$test), 0.01)` in the test sample, depending on $\lambda$
- The best $\lambda$ in the test sample is no option: an investor in `r year(test_start) - 1` does not know the test sample

::: {.highlight}
**Today:** choose $\lambda$ with the estimation sample only (cross-validation), give the penalty an economic meaning (a prior on Sharpe ratios), and ask whether the SDF is sparse in anomalies or in principal components
:::

# Cross-validation

```{r}
#| label: split-figures
#| include: false
# Consecutive blocks of the estimation sample, as in the code of the
# cross-validation slide; start and end in years, e.g. 1994.6
blocks <- estimation_months |>
  mutate(
    block = ceiling(dense_rank(date) / (n_distinct(date) / n_folds)),
    month = floor_date(date, "month")
  ) |>
  summarize(
    start = decimal_date(min(month)),
    end = decimal_date(max(month) %m+% months(1)),
    .by = block
  )
test_block <- tibble(
  start = decimal_date(test_start),
  end = decimal_date(sample_end + 1)
)
role_colors <- c(
  "Estimation" = "#b3b3b3",
  "Validation" = ku_red,
  "Test, never used for tuning" = light
)

# Rows of blocks, one row per split, coloured by their role
plot_splits <- function(plan, row_labels) {
  ggplot(
    plan,
    aes(
      xmin = start,
      xmax = end,
      ymin = row - 0.4,
      ymax = row + 0.4,
      fill = role
    )
  ) +
    geom_rect(color = "white") +
    scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(1980, 2020, by = 10)) +
    scale_y_reverse(breaks = seq_along(row_labels), labels = row_labels) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = role_colors, breaks = names(role_colors)) +
    labs(x = NULL, y = NULL, fill = NULL) +
    theme(legend.position = "bottom", panel.grid = element_blank())
}
```

## One split: estimate, validate, test

```{r}
#| label: plot-one-split
#| echo: false
#| fig-width: 11
#| fig-height: 1.7
# The last block of the estimation sample validates; the same split as fold 5
# on the next slide
blocks |>
  mutate(role = if_else(block == n_folds, "Validation", "Estimation")) |>
  summarize(start = min(start), end = max(end), .by = role) |>
  bind_rows(mutate(test_block, role = "Test, never used for tuning")) |>
  mutate(row = 1) |>
  plot_splits("One split")
```

- **Estimation block:** the weights $\hat b_\lambda$ for every $\lambda$ on the grid of lecture 10
- **Validation block:** the Sharpe ratio of each $\hat b_\lambda$. Choose the $\lambda$ with the highest
- **Test sample:** don't touch it; it judges the chosen portfolio once, at the very end
- $\lambda$ is a **hyperparameter** (or tuning parameter): not estimated with the weights, but chosen on data the weights were not estimated on

## Cross-validation for time series

```{r}
#| label: plot-folds
#| echo: false
#| fig-width: 11
#| fig-height: 3
# Each fold validates on another block and estimates on the others
expand_grid(row = seq_len(n_folds), blocks) |>
  mutate(role = if_else(row == block, "Validation", "Estimation")) |>
  bind_rows(cross_join(
    tibble(row = seq_len(n_folds), role = "Test, never used for tuning"),
    test_block
  )) |>
  plot_splits(paste("Fold", seq_len(n_folds)))
```

- $k$ = `r n_folds` consecutive blocks of the estimation sample, each one the validation block once. Choose the $\lambda$ with the highest Sharpe ratio, averaged over the $k$ validation blocks
- **Why $k$ blocks?** The Sharpe ratio of one validation block is a noisy measure (as is the RMSPE of a forecast); the average over $k$ blocks is less noisy
- Months are not shuffled into the folds: neighbouring months share news and volatility, so shuffling would leak information into the validation block
- **Downside for time series:** in folds 1 to `r n_folds - 1`, the weights are estimated partly on later months. Harmless if the return distribution is stable; if not, estimate on the past only and validate on the next block

## Cross-validation in code

::: {.panel-tabset group="language"}
## R

```{r}
#| label: cross-validation-r
#| results: hide
# k = 5 consecutive blocks of the estimation months as folds
n_folds <- 5
block_folds <- estimation_months |>
  mutate(block = ceiling(dense_rank(date) / (n_distinct(date) / n_folds))) |>
  group_vfold_cv(group = block, v = n_folds)

ridge_tuning <- tune_grid(
  ridge_workflow,
  block_folds,
  grid = tibble(penalty = ridge_lambdas),
  metrics = metric_set(sharpe_ratio)
)
ridge_fit <- ridge_workflow |>
  finalize_workflow(select_best(ridge_tuning, metric = "sharpe_ratio")) |>
  fit(estimation_months)
sharpe_in(ridge_fit, test_months)
```

## Python

#| label: cross-validation-py
#| eval: false

n_folds = 5
months = estimation_months["date"].rank("dense")
blocks = np.ceil(months / (months.max() / n_folds)).to_numpy()

ridge_search = GridSearchCV(
    ridge_model,
    {"alpha": ridge_lambdas},
    scoring=sharpe_scorer,
    cv=GroupKFold(n_splits=n_folds),
)
ridge_search.fit(x_estimation, y_estimation, groups=blocks)
sharpe_scorer(ridge_search, x_test, y_test)

:::

```{r}
#| label: chosen-penalties
#| include: false
# The lasso, tuned in the same way
lasso_tuning <- tune_grid(
  lasso_workflow,
  block_folds,
  grid = tibble(penalty = lasso_lambdas),
  metrics = metric_set(sharpe_ratio)
)
lasso_fit <- lasso_workflow |>
  finalize_workflow(select_best(lasso_tuning, metric = "sharpe_ratio")) |>
  fit(estimation_months)
ridge_lambda <- select_best(ridge_tuning, metric = "sharpe_ratio")$penalty
lasso_lambda <- select_best(lasso_tuning, metric = "sharpe_ratio")$penalty
ridge_sharpe <- sample_sharpe(ridge_fit)
lasso_sharpe <- sample_sharpe(lasso_fit)
lasso_kept <- sum(tidy(lasso_fit)$estimate != 0)
# Average Sharpe ratio of the validation blocks, by penalty
ridge_cv <- collect_metrics(ridge_tuning) |>
  arrange(penalty) |>
  pull(mean)
```

Inside, `tune_grid()` and `GridSearchCV()` loop over penalties and folds: fit on the other blocks, Sharpe ratio in the validation block, average over the folds. `GridSearchCV()` refits the best penalty by itself. The lasso the same way. Chosen: $\lambda$ = `r penalty_text(ridge_lambda)` for ridge (test Sharpe ratio `r number(ridge_sharpe[["test"]], 0.01)`), `r penalty_text(lasso_lambda)` for the lasso (`r lasso_kept` anomalies, `r number(lasso_sharpe[["test"]], 0.01)`)

# The SDF of the factor zoo

## An SDF that prices all anomalies

::: {.box}
Find the SDF $M_{t+1} = 1 - \sum_{i=1}^{N} b_i F_{i,t+1} = 1 - b'F_{t+1}$ that prices all $N$ anomalies. A long-short return costs nothing, so its price is zero: $E[M_{t+1} F_{i,t+1}] = 0$ for $i = 1, \dots, N$. Means $\mu = E[F_{t+1}]$, covariance matrix $\Sigma = \text{Var}(F_{t+1})$
:::

::: {.fragment}
$$
\begin{aligned}
E[M_{t+1} F_{t+1}] &= \mu - E[F_{t+1} F_{t+1}']\, b = 0 \\
\Longrightarrow \qquad b &= E[F_{t+1} F_{t+1}']^{-1}\mu = (\Sigma + \mu\mu')^{-1}\mu = \frac{\Sigma^{-1}\mu}{1 + \mu'\Sigma^{-1}\mu}
\end{aligned}
$$

- The SDF's loadings are proportional to $\Sigma^{-1}\mu$, the weights of the mean-variance efficient portfolio (lecture 6), whose squared Sharpe ratio is $\mu'\Sigma^{-1}\mu$: estimating the SDF and choosing the best portfolio of the zoo are the same problem
- **Why $1 - b'F$:** from now on, as in Chen, Pelger & Zhu (lecture 14), the SDF does not subtract the means. With sample moments, $\hat b = (F'F)^{-1}F'y$ is the regression of lecture 10. Kozak, Nagel & Santosh write $1 - b'(F_{t+1} - \mu)$ and get $b = \Sigma^{-1}\mu$: the same portfolio
- Each anomaly is a characteristic-managed portfolio, a long-short sort (lectures 7 and 8): $b_i$ says how much characteristic $i$ matters for prices
:::

## A prior on Sharpe ratios

::: {.box}
Kozak, Nagel & Santosh (2020): before seeing the data, an investor treats the means $\mu$ as random,

$$
\mu \sim \mathcal{N}\Big(0, \frac{\kappa^2}{\tau}\,\Sigma^2\Big)
$$

with $\Sigma^2 = \Sigma\Sigma$ and $\tau = \text{tr}(\Sigma)$, the sum of the variances. What does this prior say about the squared maximum Sharpe ratio $\mu'\Sigma^{-1}\mu$?
:::

::: {.fragment}
$$
E\big[\mu'\Sigma^{-1}\mu\big] = \text{tr}\big(\Sigma^{-1}\,\text{Var}(\mu)\big) = \frac{\kappa^2}{\tau}\,\text{tr}(\Sigma) = \kappa^2
$$

- $\kappa^2$ is the squared maximum Sharpe ratio the investor expects; $\kappa$ itself is in Sharpe ratio units
- $\Sigma^2$ instead of $\Sigma$: the prior expects large premia only from combinations of anomalies with large variance. A large Sharpe ratio from a low-variance combination is implausible
:::

## From the prior to the ridge penalty

With $T$ months of data and sample means $\hat\mu$, the posterior mean of the efficient weights $\Sigma^{-1}\mu$ is

$$
(\Sigma + \lambda I)^{-1}\hat\mu \qquad \text{with} \qquad \lambda = \frac{\tau}{\kappa^2 T}
$$

- **A ridge estimator:** with the sample covariance matrix $\hat\Sigma$ for $\Sigma$, the ridge regression of lecture 10, $(F'F + T\lambda I)^{-1}F'y = (\hat\Sigma + \hat\mu\hat\mu' + \lambda I)^{-1}\hat\mu$, is a multiple of $(\hat\Sigma + \lambda I)^{-1}\hat\mu$, as in the last step on the SDF slide: the same portfolio. The penalty is a prior about how large Sharpe ratios can be
- **From $\kappa$ to the weights:** the larger the Sharpe ratios the prior allows, the smaller $\lambda$. For $\kappa \to \infty$, the plug-in $\Sigma^{-1}\hat\mu$; for small $\kappa$, the weights shrink towards zero, proportional to $\hat\mu$
- More months $T$ also lower $\lambda$: the more data, the less the prior matters

## The prior behind cross-validation

```{r}
#| label: implied-kappa
#| include: false
# The annual maximum Sharpe ratio that the prior expects for each penalty
x_estimation <- as.matrix(estimation_months[anomaly_names])
tau <- sum(diag(cov(x_estimation)))
implied_kappa <- function(lambda) {
  sqrt(tau / (lambda * nrow(x_estimation)) * months_per_year)
}
kappa_path <- ridge_path |>
  mutate(kappa = implied_kappa(lambda), cv = ridge_cv) |>
  filter(lambda > 0)

# Ridge on second moments (the closed form of lecture 10) and the posterior
# mean differ only by a scale factor (Sherman-Morrison), so they are the same
# portfolio. The glmnet fit matches the closed form up to its threshold
covariance <- cov(x_estimation) * (nrow(x_estimation) - 1) / nrow(x_estimation)
posterior_weights <- solve(
  covariance + ridge_lambda * diag(ncol(x_estimation)),
  colMeans(x_estimation)
)
closed_form_weights <- solve(
  crossprod(x_estimation) +
    nrow(x_estimation) * ridge_lambda * diag(ncol(x_estimation)),
  colSums(x_estimation)
)
weight_ratio <- closed_form_weights / posterior_weights
stopifnot(sd(weight_ratio) / mean(weight_ratio) < 1e-6)
ridge_fit_weights <- tidy(ridge_fit) |>
  filter(term != "(Intercept)") |>
  pull(estimate)
stopifnot(cor(ridge_fit_weights, closed_form_weights) > 1 - 1e-6)
```

```{r}
#| label: plot-kappa
#| echo: false
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 4.2
sample_labels <- c(
  estimation = paste("Estimation", estimation_years),
  cv = paste("Cross-validation: average of the", n_folds, "validation blocks"),
  test = paste("Test", test_years)
)
chosen_kappa <- implied_kappa(ridge_lambda)

kappa_path |>
  select(kappa, cv, estimation, test) |>
  pivot_longer(-kappa, names_to = "sample", values_to = "sharpe") |>
  mutate(sample = factor(sample_labels[sample], levels = sample_labels)) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = kappa, y = sharpe, color = sample)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = chosen_kappa, linetype = "dashed", color = grey) +
  annotate(
    "text",
    x = chosen_kappa * 0.9,
    y = max(kappa_path$estimation),
    label = "Chosen by cross-validation",
    hjust = 1,
    color = grey
  ) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  scale_x_log10() +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("#b3b3b3", jet, ku_red)) +
  labs(
    x = "κ, the root of the squared maximum Sharpe ratio the prior expects (annualized)",
    y = "Sharpe ratio (annualized)",
    color = NULL
  ) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

- The cross-validated $\lambda$ = `r penalty_text(ridge_lambda)` means $\kappa \approx$ **`r number(implied_kappa(ridge_lambda), 0.1)`** a year: a prior that expects maximum Sharpe ratios of about this size. Still optimistic, but far below the plug-in's `r number(plug_in_sharpe[["estimation"]], 0.1)`
- Same portfolio as ridge on the regression of lecture 10; the weights differ only by a scale factor. The prior is the reason for the penalty, not a new method

# Is the SDF sparse?

## Principal components

::: {.box}
Find the portfolio $v_1$ of the anomalies with the largest variance, $\max_v v'\Sigma v$ subject to $v'v = 1$. Then $v_2$, the portfolio with the largest variance that is uncorrelated with $v_1$, and so on
:::

::: {.fragment}
$$
\Sigma v_j = \delta_j v_j \qquad P_{j,t} = v_j'F_t \qquad \text{Var}(P_{j,t}) = \delta_j
$$

- The weights $v_j$ are the eigenvectors of $\Sigma$, the variances $\delta_j$ its eigenvalues (lecture 4). `r length(anomaly_names)` anomalies give `r length(anomaly_names)` principal components, uncorrelated with each other
- Nothing is lost: with $V = (v_1, \dots, v_N)$ and $V'V = I$, the components are $P_t = V'F_t$ and the anomalies $F_t = V P_t$
- An SDF in components is an SDF in anomalies: $M_{t+1} = 1 - b_P'P_{t+1} = 1 - (V b_P)'F_{t+1}$, so the anomalies get the weights $b = V b_P$
:::

## Two anomalies, two components

```{r}
#| label: momentum-components
#| include: false
# Two momentum anomalies: the returns of the past 12 and 6 months
momentum_names <- c(Mom12m = "12-month momentum", Mom6m = "6-month momentum")
momentum <- as.matrix(estimation_months[names(momentum_names)])
momentum_test <- as.matrix(test_months[names(momentum_names)])
momentum_eigen <- eigen(cov(momentum), symmetric = TRUE)
# Eigenvectors have no sign: both buy 12-month momentum
momentum_vectors <- sweep(
  momentum_eigen$vectors,
  2,
  sign(momentum_eigen$vectors[1, ]),
  `*`
)
momentum_variance_share <- momentum_eigen$values / sum(momentum_eigen$values)
momentum_sharpe <- map(1:2, \(j) {
  c(
    estimation = sharpe_ratio_vec(
      estimate = momentum %*% momentum_vectors[, j]
    ),
    test = sharpe_ratio_vec(estimate = momentum_test %*% momentum_vectors[, j])
  )
})
momentum_correlation <- cor(momentum)[1, 2]
```

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="45%"}
```{r}
#| label: plot-momentum-components
#| echo: false
#| fig-width: 5
#| fig-height: 5
# Each component as a line through the mean; both lines have the same length,
# so the cloud of points shows the difference in variance
line_length <- 15
momentum_points <- as_tibble(momentum * 100)
momentum_lines <- tibble(
  component = c("First component", "Second component"),
  x = mean(momentum_points$Mom6m) - line_length * momentum_vectors[2, ],
  y = mean(momentum_points$Mom12m) - line_length * momentum_vectors[1, ],
  xend = mean(momentum_points$Mom6m) + line_length * momentum_vectors[2, ],
  yend = mean(momentum_points$Mom12m) + line_length * momentum_vectors[1, ]
)

ggplot(momentum_points, aes(x = Mom6m, y = Mom12m)) +
  geom_point(color = "#b3b3b3", alpha = 0.7) +
  geom_segment(
    data = momentum_lines,
    aes(x = x, y = y, xend = xend, yend = yend),
    color = ku_red,
    linewidth = 1.2
  ) +
  # First component: label at its lower end; second: at its upper end
  geom_text(
    data = momentum_lines,
    aes(
      x = c(x[1], xend[2]),
      y = c(y[1], yend[2]),
      label = component
    ),
    color = ku_red,
    size = 4.5,
    hjust = c(-0.08, 0.5),
    vjust = c(0.5, -0.6)
  ) +
  coord_equal() +
  labs(
    x = paste(momentum_names[["Mom6m"]], "(% per month)"),
    y = paste(momentum_names[["Mom12m"]], "(% per month)")
  )
```
:::

::: {.column width="55%"}
- Monthly returns `r estimation_years`, correlation `r number(momentum_correlation, 0.01)`
- **First component:** both anomalies, weights `r number(momentum_vectors[1, 1], 0.01)` and `r number(momentum_vectors[2, 1], 0.01)`. `r percent(momentum_variance_share[1])` of the variance, Sharpe ratio `r number(momentum_sharpe[[1]][["estimation"]], 0.01)`
- **Second component:** 12-month minus 6-month momentum, weights `r number(momentum_vectors[1, 2], 0.01)` and `r number(momentum_vectors[2, 2], 0.01, style_negative = "minus")`. Only `r percent(momentum_variance_share[2])` of the variance, but Sharpe ratio `r number(momentum_sharpe[[2]][["estimation"]], 0.01)`
- The prior of Kozak, Nagel & Santosh doubts the second: in `r test_years` its Sharpe ratio is `r number(momentum_sharpe[[2]][["test"]], 0.01, style_negative = "minus")`
:::

## The lasso on principal components

- Kozak, Nagel & Santosh (2020): an SDF with a few anomalies prices badly; an SDF with a few **principal components** of the anomalies prices well
- `pc_lasso_weights()`: the components $P_t = V'F_t$ of the months it is fitted on, the lasso of lecture 10 on them, and their weights on the anomalies, $b = V b_P$

::: {.panel-tabset group="language"}
## R

```{r}
#| label: pc-lasso-r
pc_lasso_weights <- function(months, lambda) {
  x <- as.matrix(months[anomaly_names])
  components <- eigen(cov(x), symmetric = TRUE)$vectors
  lasso_fit <- lasso_model |>
    finalize_model(tibble(penalty = lambda)) |>
    fit_xy(as.data.frame(x %*% components), months$y)
  components %*% tidy(lasso_fit)$estimate[-1]
}
```

## Python

```{python}
#| label: pc-lasso-py
#| eval: false
def pc_lasso_weights(x, y, lam):
    _, components = np.linalg.eigh(np.cov(x, rowvar=False))
    lasso = clone(lasso_model).set_params(alpha=lam).fit(x @ components, y)
    return components @ lasso.coef_
```
:::

**Why a function of our own:** `step_pca()` (tidymodels) and `PCA()` (scikit-learn) take the eigenvectors of $F'F$ instead of $\hat\Sigma$ or subtract the average returns, the premia the SDF prices. The function is cross-validated with the folds and the metric of `tune_grid()`

## Cross-validation by hand

::: {.panel-tabset group="language"}
## R

```{r}
#| label: pc-lasso-cv-r
# The loop inside tune_grid(): for each penalty and fold, fit on the
# estimation blocks, Sharpe ratio in the validation block
pc_lasso_cv <- map_dbl(lasso_lambdas, \(lambda) {
  map_dbl(block_folds$splits, \(split) {
    weights <- pc_lasso_weights(analysis(split), lambda)
    validation <- assessment(split)
    portfolio_returns <- as.matrix(validation[anomaly_names]) %*% weights
    sharpe_ratio_vec(validation$y, portfolio_returns[, 1])
  }) |>
    mean()
})
pc_lasso_lambda <- lasso_lambdas[which.max(pc_lasso_cv)]
```

## Python

```{python}
#| label: pc-lasso-cv-py
#| eval: false
# The loop inside GridSearchCV(): for each penalty and fold, fit on the
# estimation blocks, Sharpe ratio in the validation block
x, y = x_estimation.to_numpy(), y_estimation.to_numpy()
folds = list(GroupKFold(n_splits=n_folds).split(x, y, blocks))
pc_lasso_cv = []
for lam in lasso_lambdas:
    sharpes = []
    for fit_rows, validation_rows in folds:
        weights = pc_lasso_weights(x[fit_rows], y[fit_rows], lam)
        portfolio_returns = x[validation_rows] @ weights
        sharpes.append(sharpe_ratio(y[validation_rows], portfolio_returns))
    pc_lasso_cv.append(np.mean(sharpes))
pc_lasso_lambda = lasso_lambdas[np.argmax(pc_lasso_cv)]
```
:::

```{r}
#| label: pc-chosen
#| include: false
# The lasso on the components of the whole estimation sample
components_estimation <- eigen(cov(x_estimation), symmetric = TRUE)$vectors
pc_lasso_fit <- function(lambda) {
  lasso_model |>
    finalize_model(tibble(penalty = lambda)) |>
    fit_xy(
      as.data.frame(x_estimation %*% components_estimation),
      estimation_months$y
    )
}
pc_kept <- sum(tidy(pc_lasso_fit(pc_lasso_lambda))$estimate[-1] != 0)
```

`pc_lasso_weights()` computes $V$ from the estimation blocks only, so the validation block cannot shape the components. Chosen: $\lambda$ = `r penalty_text(pc_lasso_lambda)`, which keeps **`r pc_kept`** of the `r length(anomaly_names)` components

## Sparse in what?

```{r}
#| label: sparsity-paths
#| include: false
x_test <- as.matrix(test_months[anomaly_names])
weights_sharpe <- function(weights) {
  c(
    estimation = sharpe_ratio_vec(estimate = drop(x_estimation %*% weights)),
    test = sharpe_ratio_vec(estimate = drop(x_test %*% weights))
  )
}
sparsity <- bind_rows(
  map(lasso_lambdas, \(lambda) {
    fit <- lasso_workflow |>
      finalize_workflow(tibble(penalty = lambda)) |>
      fit(estimation_months)
    tibble(
      inputs = "Anomalies",
      lambda = lambda,
      kept = sum(tidy(fit)$estimate != 0),
      !!!sample_sharpe(fit)
    )
  }),
  map(lasso_lambdas, \(lambda) {
    pc_weights <- tidy(pc_lasso_fit(lambda))$estimate[-1]
    tibble(
      inputs = "Principal components",
      lambda = lambda,
      kept = sum(pc_weights != 0),
      !!!weights_sharpe(components_estimation %*% pc_weights)
    )
  })
)
pc_chosen <- sparsity |>
  filter(inputs == "Principal components", lambda == pc_lasso_lambda)
anomaly_chosen <- sparsity |>
  filter(inputs == "Anomalies", lambda == lasso_lambda)
```

```{r}
#| label: plot-sparsity
#| echo: false
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 3.9
chosen <- bind_rows(anomaly_chosen, pc_chosen)
ggplot(sparsity, aes(x = kept, y = test, color = inputs)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_point(
    data = chosen,
    size = 5,
    shape = 21,
    stroke = 1.3,
    fill = NA,
    show.legend = FALSE
  ) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c(jet, ku_red)) +
  labs(
    x = "Number of anomalies or principal components with a non-zero weight",
    y = paste0("Sharpe ratio ", test_years, "\n(annualized)"),
    color = "Lasso on",
    caption = "Circles: penalty chosen by cross-validation"
  ) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

- On our zoo, the principal components are **not** sparser: `r pc_chosen$kept` principal components give `r number(pc_chosen$test, 0.01)` in the test sample, `r anomaly_chosen$kept` anomalies give `r number(anomaly_chosen$test, 0.01)`
- Neither is sparse: a good SDF of the zoo needs dozens of anomalies or components, not a handful
- Different from Kozak, Nagel & Santosh, who find a few principal components enough: they combine the lasso with their ridge prior and judge the SDF by how well it prices the anomalies, not by its Sharpe ratio

## Beyond one SDF: averaging over models

- Every penalty, every set of anomalies is one model of the SDF. Which one is right is uncertain, too
- **Bayesian model averaging** (Bryzgalova, Huang & Julliard, 2023; Avramov, Cheng, Metzker & Voigt, 2023): weight every combination of factors by its posterior probability and average the SDFs
- Bryzgalova, Huang & Julliard: no small set of factors dominates; the averaged SDF is dense

- Every penalty chosen by cross-validation in the estimation sample
